transverse electron momentum in the tunneling regime is strongly suppressed with increasing ellipticity, while it is enhanced in the over the barrier ionizations.

the transverse electron motion in the strong field atomic ionisation process.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the transverse momentum distribution is a very sensitive tool to distinguish between the two regimes of strong-field ionization.

in tunneling ionization regime the transverse electron momenta are distributed around the direction of laser polarization and the distribution width decreases when ellipticity increases, while in over the barrier ionizations the transverse electron moments are distributed around the directions of laser electric field vectors and the distribution width increases when ellipticity increases.

in tunneling regime the ellipticity parameter does not affect the shape of transverse electron momentum distributions while in over the barrier ionizations the transverse electron momenta are strongly dependent on ellipticity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the ellipticity of the driving laser pulses plays an important role in the ionization process, and the ellipticity parameter is a key factor in the ionization dynamics.
the transverse momentum distribution is more sensitive to the ellipticity of the laser field in the tunneling ionization regime than in over the barrier ionizations.
the transverse momentum distribution in the over the barrier ionizaton regime is more sensitive to ellipticity of the driving field.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the transverse momentum distribution of the tunneling electrons, which is typically assumed to be a Gaussian, becomes non-Gaussian as the ellipticity parameter is increased.
